topPRs.title: feat(cloud): claim backup work without shard starvation
topPRs.author: standujar
topPRs.body:
# Relates to

Relates to #24407 and epic #20726. Depends on Draft #29694.

This Draft adds the bounded claimant/recovery authority only. It does not activate a production caller, reserve catalogue entries, invoke a provider, mutate capacity, trigger autoscale, deploy, or retire the legacy scheduler.

- [x] This PR is intentionally stacked on `feat/24407-backup-admission-enrollment-repository-v4`.
- [x] The exact stacked base and current `origin/develop` were revalidated with zero conflicts.
- [x] Exact-head affected tests and `bun run verify:cloud` passed.

# Risks

Medium. Claiming coordinates concurrent workers across 64 shards and strict tenant/node lanes. A defect could duplicate leases, starve a shard, cross an expired fence, or violate priority ordering. Durable frozen recovery cursors, trigger guards, post-lock database time, exact generation/attempt fences, and bounded `SKIP LOCKED` scans constrain those risks.

# What does this PR do?

- Claims queued `schedule_capture / reserve_capture` work with strict business-priority passes.
- Uses maximum-cardinality tenant/node lane matching without deriving authority from opaque work UUIDs.
- Adds durable, monotone recovery high-water/cursor state for deferred and expired work.
- Advances recovery and shard service turns even when raw rows are locked, preserving cross-shard fairness.
- Fences heartbeat, defer, and settlement against the exact live generation, attempt, cycle, and post-lock database clock.
- Adds real PostgreSQL and PGlite coverage, including 10,000 due rows plus 640 arrivals across all 64 shards.
- Performs database-only admission changes; capacity/autoscale/provider sentinels remain unchanged.

# Testing

Exact candidate: `6431ebd5052479e87e1112267c389d7093162bd4`

Exact stacked base: `087b75a5bd0e66f70070bd5c0c0cbc8158dc289d`

Validated `origin/develop`: `6e8882b47c3f4f242d2a3c655d287f2969d00595`

Bun 1.3.14:

- Real PostgreSQL 16 claimant suite: 12/12 tests, 96 assertions.
- PGlite claimant + matching + migration suites: 45/45 tests, 307 assertions.
- `bun run verify:cloud`: 84/84 tasks, exit 0.
- `bun run --cwd packages/cloud/shared db:check-migrations`: passed.
- Targeted Biome, actionlint, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Fresh independent exact-SHA adversarial review: no P0, P1, or P2 findings.

topPRs.title: feat(wechat): direct Official Account + WeCom first-party paths (#24371)
topPRs.author: HomunculusLabs
topPRs.body:
# feat(wechat): direct Official Account + WeCom first-party paths (#24371)

Closes #24371

Replaces the removed third-party proxy transport with direct first-party WeChat paths: Official Account (MP) and WeCom self-built apps over the official platform APIs — signature-verified public callback server, official customer-service/app-message sends, no proxy.

## What changes

- **Direct transports** — `api-client.ts` / `token-manager.ts` (account-scoped access tokens, single-flight) send through fixed `api.weixin.qq.com` / `qyapi.weixin.qq.com` hosts; personal/proxy/wecom-third-party modes rejected with typed errors; legacy `WECHAT_API_KEY`/`WECHAT_PROXY_URL` fail with `WECHAT_PROXY_CONFIG_UNSUPPORTED`.
- **Callback boundary** — `callback-server.ts` + `callback-crypto.ts`: SHA-1 signature verification before any parsing; AES-256-CBC encrypted mode with Tencent's 32-byte PKCS#7 scheme; receiver-id binding (corpId / gh_ original ID — never appId); per-account path addressing so a ciphertext signed for one account is never accepted for another.
- **Hardened XML** — `xml.ts` flat parser (CDATA leaves, no DTD/entities/nesting/duplicate roots), parsed only after signature verification.
- **Connector + account provider** — targets derived exclusively from signature-verified inbound senders (no roster API on these platforms); observational account status (connected requires a real first-party observation).
- **Tests** — 16 new tests across 6 suites (config resolution, callback boundary with real listeners, crypto with official Tencent vectors, UTF-8 chunk-boundary integrity, token lifecycle, provider), all with RED controls per review round.

## Key invariants

- Signature verification precedes payload parsing; encrypted-mode accounts cannot be downgraded to the plaintext path by request shape.
- Outbound receipts are enforced: platform rejection, non-zero errcode, or unparseable body is a failed send — never a fabricated success.
- Replay expiry aligns with the timestamp freshness endpoint (r5 fix).

## Verification

|---|---|
| `plugin-wechat` typecheck | 0 errors |
| Full plugin suite (fresh capture at publish) | 96/96 |

topPRs.title: fix(reminders): restore Shared and Dedicated mutation parity
topPRs.author: standujar
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- align the Shared reminder action with Dedicated lifecycle basics: create, list, update, snooze, complete, delete/dismiss, and confirmation-gated clear
- deduplicate semantic creates across message ids and transport retries, including relative schedules and pre-patch rows
- update reminders through a receipt-backed replacement, coalesce exact duplicates, and return honest partial outcomes
- keep reminder delivery scoped to the verified DM or immutable group authority
- render local time before UTC, canonicalize IANA timezones, and reject offset-less absolute timestamps
- route the exact production phrases to REMINDERS ahead of TODO, buffer required actions before streaming, and surface verified failures instead of silent 500 turns
- add server-owned intent and provenance fences so planner operation drift cannot bypass clear confirmation or mutate an unrelated reminder

## Verified production evidence

The read-only production audit found two semantically identical reminders created eighteen seconds apart with different message-derived idempotency keys. Both fired and dispatched successfully. Later delete/clear turns reached Personal Shared but failed before any reply or trace persistence.

No production data, reminder, deployment, configuration, or infrastructure was changed during the audit.

## Safety

- clear-all requires the exact preceding server challenge, a full explicit confirmation, and the confirmed action parameter
- clock corrections require a grounded scheduling confirmation and cannot reuse fresh-create language
- explicit list/create mismatches fail closed before scheduler access
- malformed or cross-destination reminder rows remain unreachable
- diagnostic reporting is best-effort and excludes message text and resource identifiers

## Validation

- focused scheduling, reminder, and action behavior: 327 passed
- SQL persistence: 17 passed
- plugin scheduling: 624 passed
- chat/history behavior: 56 passed
- integration coverage: 6 passed
- package typechecks, changed-file lint, build, and `git diff --check`: clean

The current CI failures are outside this PR's changed paths:

- `Source static smoke` reached existing `@elizaos/ui` design-contract graph checks; two checks expected zero findings and observed four.
- the Windows security job was cancelled while installing workspace dependencies after roughly 33 minutes; every security step was skipped.
- the aggregate admission check is red because those two lanes did not succeed.

Billing payment replay E2E is green.

Closes #29688

This PR targets develop. It has not been deployed or merged.

topPRs.title: feat(core,plugin-sql): native paging for large messages and attachment text (#25140)
topPRs.author: HomunculusLabs
topPRs.body:
# feat(core,plugin-sql): native paging for large messages and attachment text (#25140)

Closes #25140

Adds native content segmentation and paging so large message bodies and attachment text are stored as revision-fenced segments and paged on demand, instead of being written and read as single unbounded rows.

## What changes

- **`packages/core/src/memory/content-segmentation.ts` (new)** — segmentation contracts: bounded segment emission, surrogate-safe boundaries, deterministic segment identity; 14 unit tests.
- **`core memory.ts` / `types/database.ts`** — `getMemoryContentPage` paging read path; message/readAttachment actions consume pages instead of whole rows.
- **`plugin-sql` schema + store (new: `memoryTextSegments`)** — generation-addressed segments with revision fencing: `createMemory` publishes segments with a bounded marker, `updateMemory` replaces the generation and retires the stale one, large-to-small replacement retires the descriptor, deletion cascades; small content stays inline (fallback path returns null pages); large attachment text without an id or with duplicate ids is rejected.
- **Real-runtime suites (new)** — 10 real PGlite tests: parent-first publication, paging with revision fencing, reassembly across restart, atomic generation replacement, legacy large-unsegmented row flagging, owner-bound attachment paging, access-context probe coverage, rollback atomicity.

## Key invariants

- Pages are revision-fenced: a reader can never reassemble content mixing two generations.
- Generation replacement is atomic and retires the prior generation — stale segments are never served after an update.
- Legacy large unsegmented rows are flagged, not silently repaged; small rows pass through inline.

## Test-lane disclosure

Nine of the ten new plugin-sql tests live in `*.real.test.ts` files, which the PR vitest lane deliberately excludes (`plugins/plugin-sql/src/vitest.config.ts`, #10104) — they run on the post-merge lane (`VITEST_LANE=post-merge` / `TEST_LANE=post-merge`) and in the captures below. The pre-merge green checks therefore reflect the non-real suites (core unit + surface + probe tests), not the real-PGlite fencing behavior; see the backend-logs capture for the real-suite evidence. The post-merge lane does execute plugin-sql real suites.

## Verification

# feat(discord): publish account-scoped room membership evidence

Closes #24365

Replaces the false `rooms[0]` WORLD_CONNECTED roster mapping with permission-aware, account-scoped Discord room membership evidence published to the canonical `MembershipService` contract (#24246: `packages/core/src/types/membership.ts` + plugin-sql `sql-membership`).

## What changes

- **`membership.ts` (new, 991 lines)** — membership evidence engine: permission-aware small-guild snapshot collection, sender renewals, member/permission/reconnect deltas, multi-account identity scoping, typed error classification (`ElizaError.code` first).
- **`membership-bridge.ts` (new, 600 lines)** — bridges discord.js guild/member/role events onto canonical `MembershipRecord` commands (`applyCompleteMembershipSnapshot`, `reportIncompleteMembershipSnapshot`).
- **`discord-events.ts` (+467)** — wires guildMemberAdd/Remove/Update, roleUpdate, permission changes, and shard resume into the bridge.
- **`service.ts` (+342)** — publishes evidence per account; small-guild snapshots are complete; partial/large/missing-intent/fetch failures degrade to `unavailable` — never an empty roster implying mass removal.
- **`discord-interactions.ts` (+61/−31)** — WORLD_CONNECTED standardized payload no longer asserts a `rooms[0]`-derived roster.
- **`membership-adapters.ts` (new)** — adapter seam between discord.js types and canonical scope identity.
- **`discord-commands.ts` (+15)** — operator command to force a reconciliation snapshot.
- **Tests (new suites)** — `membership-authority.real.test.ts` (969 lines: real MembershipService over the plugin-sql store, deterministic permission matrices, multi-account isolation, stale-evidence-never-removes) and `membership-shard-lifecycle.test.ts` (236 lines: shard degrade/resume + facade hook forwarding, RED-proven 4/4 pre-fix at 9b9c9464b8).

## Key invariants

- Partial, failed, large-guild (no `GUILD_MEMBERS` intent), or disconnected evidence is reported `unavailable`/`incomplete` — it never implies removals.
- Shard-scoped degrade: only guilds owned by the dead shard degrade; other accounts' evidence stays current (worldIds filter, RED control 2/2).
- Guild-owner `PermissionsBitField.All` survives role aggregation (owner preserve, RED control 2/2).
- Multi-account: per-account service facade forwards all five membership hooks with the account id (RED control 1/5 pre-fix → 5/5).

## Verification
